adjudicated_statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Write (CE) for the standard degree-four Casnati–Ekedahl ideal resolution 0→O_X(-4)⊗p^*det F→O_X(-2)⊗p^*F→I_C→0 on X=P(E^∨) with p_*O_X(1)=E, and (N) for the weak relative-canonical normalization O_X(1)|_C ≅ ω_{C/P^1}⊗γ^*A for some A∈Pic(P^1). The fibrewise identifications (1.4) and (2.1) and the quadric criterion (3.3) of ATT-0100 are derived only under (CE)+(N) with h^0(L)=3. An existence clause asserting that a concrete smooth genus-six finite flat degree-four cover γ:C→P^1 satisfies (CE) and (N) and is balanced cannot establish those conclusions by invoking (3.3) or (2.1) unless the Casnati–Ekedahl embedding, the two-term resolution, and the restriction in (N) are independently constructed for that cover or imported from a cited theorem that applies to it. ATT-0100 Section 10 and CLM-0100-12 / theorem A5 do not discharge this requirement for the proposed genus-two intermediate example (C→C'' a double cover of a general genus-two curve, branched along a general member of |δ^2| for general δ∈Pic^3(C''), γ the composite with the hyperelliptic pencil of C'', and Γ the ramification divisor): the text constructs the curve, pencil, section counts, and involution, then applies (3.3) and (2.1) without constructing or citing the embedding, resolution, or (N). By contrast, CLM-0100-6 and CLM-0100-7 correctly leave balancedness of the bielliptic-composed and (1,2)-(2,2) complete-intersection examples conditional on (CE)+(N). Independently, Casnati–Ekedahl 1996 Theorem 2.1 supplies, for every finite flat Gorenstein cover of degree d≥3, the relative-canonical embedding induced by α^*E→ω_α and the Casnati–Ekedahl resolution; for d=4 this is a two-term resolution of I_C, and Canning–Larson arXiv:2208.02357v2 Lemma 10.6 records O_{P(E^∨)}(1)|_C ≅ ω_C⊗γ^*ω_{P^1}^∨. The genus-two composite is such a cover, so (CE) and the strong form of (N) (A trivial) hold for it by that general theorem if cited; this statement does not assert that the geometric example fails to be Gorenstein or that the involution or section counts are false. Those citations are absent from ATT-0100, so CLM-0100-12 remains unresolved as written. Future attempts may discharge (CE)+(N) for this example by citing Casnati–Ekedahl Theorem 2.1, but must still separately justify applying (3.3) to conclude balancedness.
contradiction_resolution: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the finding does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001–THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with corroborated FND-0105 (keep every clause using the weak CE relative-canonical normalization explicitly conditional, or add one cited source line), FND-0137 (a genus-six automorphism can fix six marked points, so a nontrivial ordered stabilizer is possible), and FND-0142 (balanced constancy of h^0 excludes only the hyperelliptic-composed pencil). Mandatory first reads of ATT-0100 and REV-0149 confirm the exact contested passage: ATT-0100 Section 0 carries (CE) and (N) as standing hypotheses that are never asserted, derives (1.4), (2.1) and the quadric criterion (3.3) only under those hypotheses, and in Section 6 correctly leaves the bielliptic and (1,2)-(2,2) examples conditional on (CE)+(N) (CLM-0100-6, CLM-0100-7). Section 10 and CLM-0100-12 / theorem A5 then assert existence of pairs satisfying (CE)+(BAL)+(N) for the genus-two double-cover composite by invoking (3.3) after only curve, pencil, section-count, and involution checks; REV-0149 therefore marks CLM-0100-12 unresolved and the attempt incomplete. Live primary check: Casnati–Ekedahl 1996 Theorem 2.1, as quoted in Patel arXiv:1508.06016 Theorem 1.6 and Bujokas–Patel arXiv:1504.03756 Theorem 2.1, applies to every finite flat Gorenstein cover of degree d≥3 and supplies both the embedding induced by α^*E→ω_α and the Casnati–Ekedahl resolution (for d=4 a two-term resolution of I_C by π^*F(-2) and π^*det F(-4)). Canning–Larson arXiv:2208.02357v2 Lemma 10.6 (proof) records the matching packet convention O_{P(E^∨)}(1)|_C ≅ ω_C ⊗ γ^*ω_{P^1}^∨, citing the same theorem, together with deg(W_{f_i}|_C)=4g+12-4f_i. The proposed genus-two composite is a smooth, hence Gorenstein, finite flat degree-four cover of P^1, so (CE) and the strong form of (N) (A trivial) are theorems for it if that citation is made. ATT-0100 does not make it: SRC-0004 is used only for the packet excerpt’s sign convention and degree formulae, the excerpt omits the restriction sentence, and FND-0105 still records (N) as an undischarged campaign hypothesis. The circularity is therefore a genuine obstruction to treating CLM-0100-12 as proved, not a claim that the geometric cover lacks (CE) or (N). Distinct from FND-0105; do not merge. Promote the narrowed statement.
